output.subject: We have received your complaint about calls to your number
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us. We have received your complaint, and we want to confirm the main points as you described them.

You told us that you are not a Meridian Harbor Bank customer, but that for about a month you have been receiving calls meant for someone else about a past-due auto loan. You mentioned that you have told callers at least five times that they have the wrong number, and that the calls have continued. You also told us that during yesterday's call, the caller shared details about another person's balance and the possible collection of their car. You feel this is information you should never have been given.

You asked that your number be removed from our call list, and that any contact with you be made in writing.

We're sorry to hear about the frustration you've described. Your complaint is being reviewed, and we will respond to you within 10 business days.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: The customer says they are not a Meridian Harbor Bank customer. Confirm that before replying.
Check the name tokens. The sign-off reads '⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧, B. ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_2⟧', so the greeting token may not resolve to the right name.
The customer's written contact detail appears to have been tokenized as ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧. Confirm the correct email or postal address and reply only by that written channel.
Decide how to handle the request to remove the number from the call list. The draft acknowledges the request but makes no commitment.
The customer reports that a third party's debt details (balance and possible repossession) were disclosed to them. This needs specialist assessment.
The customer reports that calls continued after at least five wrong-number notices. Verify this against call records.
Do not add the debtor's name, balance or loan details to the reply, since the recipient is reportedly not the account holder.
Do not include the customer's phone number in the reply.
Acknowledge-only replies normally tell the customer a specialist team is reviewing the complaint; this reply does not mention any team. Confirm that wording is intended.
